items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Rosie Clooney’s a good friend of mine

ctx.x: So like “All the Things You Are,” tunes like that, the stuff from The Real Book, or the third of it that people really play, those tunes were being played on the radio by artists —

Oh you heard them constantly. I mean don’t forget, pop radio in those days, in the ‘40’s and ‘50s, this was, I mean in the ‘40s, all it was was big bands and maybe some corny pop songs. I don’t want to put anybody down but like Rosie Clooney’s a good friend of mine, but her “Come Ona My House” songs in that category, which seemed to be the pop. But in spite of that there was all these wonderful songs from Broadway and the standards, and Irving Berlin and Porter and everybody. That’s all you heard on the radio.…
Eventually you went to New York?
